title: Finite-Tor constructible complexes are compact in the étale derived category
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite $\ell$-primary ring and $X$ a scheme of the standing setting (finite type over the base
field, so all $\operatorname{cd}_\ell$ are finite). Every $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ is compact in
$\D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$: for every family $(K_s)$ in $\D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$,
$\bigoplus_s\Hom(C,K_s)\to\Hom(C,\bigoplus_sK_s)$ is an isomorphism.

Here the standing field is $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; $A$ is commutative and $\ell^rA=0$ for some $r\geq0$, as in the parent proposition. The category $\D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ is the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Its full subcategory $\Dctf$ consists of objects with bounded constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and Tor amplitude in some finite interval [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Compactness and the indexing universe are those of [def-pc-compact-object; def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Apply the first clause of [lem-pur-etale-finite-ring-compact-generators] with $T=X$ and $C=A$. Its hypotheses hold: the standing field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] is algebraically closed; $\ell\ne p=\operatorname{char}k$, so $\ell$ is invertible in $k$; $X$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme, and no separatedness is required there; $A$ is a finite commutative ring with $\ell^rA=0$. Its category is the same ordinary unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Its bounded constructible condition is the item's: only finitely many nonzero $H^i$, each constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Its finite Tor amplitude condition, $H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AN)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $N$ and $i\notin[r,s]$, is the condition of [def-kun-tor-amplitude] for some finite interval. Compactness is that of [def-pc-compact-object] for set-indexed families in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Hence every $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ is compact in $\D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Edge cases are included in that statement: the empty scheme and the zero ring give the zero category, in which every map is an isomorphism, and the empty family gives the comparison $0\to\operatorname{Hom}(C,0)=0$.
